title: Say. If you made fun, good game with AI. what stop another just clone it and sell it cheaper.
author: More_Setting4514
selftext:
Yeah. AI not just prompt "make a fun game". I know  
But AI read your chat log 

Your design, your intention or whatever is saved. So if someone say copy xyz game they AI will likely use the data of xyz devs to clone it.

So that argument don't hold for me.

comments.author: Original-League-6094
comments.body: Nothing. Most of us are here because we enjoy making little games or because we are making the game we want to play. Not many here are looking to make commercial hits.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
before AI, you can make a clone of any games you want and sell it.

in fact, thats what many companies and people do: they just make clones and push them out as mobile games, browser games. 

so the answer is "nothing"

i.e. ever since dark souls got popular, we got a million soul-likes. it is what it is

replies.author: More_Setting4514
replies.body:
but they need time to clone before. At least few months.

So if you make a game, you have few months to sell it. Which is enough. Most game sale drop after 1 or 2 months.

Now? They can clone it in a week.

replies.author: Impressive_Award_679
replies.body: If its a good AA or a AAA game no AI can copy it 20% as good as the original. It will just not sell well. U can do it, but it will be a waste of time in the future. For sure not in a week. Even astra isnt really able to get 3D modells animations as good as even good indie artists in less than 3 days.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
You are underestimating how cheap/fast contractors work. It doesnt take a few months lol

The only difference now is that a random person can use ai to join the fun. That's it really

The market was really saturated even before AI. I think most people just weren't paying attention because they weren't making games themselves

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: You can copy/reverse engineer whatever you want, but the work starts after that. A game isn‘t a one-hit(/prompt)-wonder.

replies.author: More_Setting4514
replies.body:
Like I said, AI read your log chat.

So your prompt to make a A game will be saved.

So when another dev prompt "make a clone A game"

AI will read a chat log from dev A and bring it to your game.

Maybe not work wonder in first hit but very likely it is workable.

replies.body: This is not how AI works…

replies.body: Fr there’s more consumers than there are people who want to go through the headache of being a game dev/thinking like one. This shit takes a lot of thought out executions. But to go ahead and be blunt, whatever game you wanna release do it cuz I don’t think anyone would wanna clone it @op

comments.author: freshposthistory
comments.body: It’s all over anyways just enjoy the tool before games are pointless

comments.author: Netherium
comments.body: I would be honored if I made a game so damn fun, people tried to make their own version of it. I would just hope the evolve it and take it to the next level.

comments.author: RoryOS
comments.body:
What's stopping a human from lifting your idea either. My game is months in the works. The barrier is the effort to make it, but it's easily overcome. 

What I'm making actually is a clone of the 90s tomb raider games. I don't even have a char log to lift from. I've just broken down the mechanics I want and implemented them over by one

comments.author: because-potato
comments.body:
It still takes time to make a unique game. 

I’m making a very unique mobile MMORPG and I’ve been making it for a month now with no end in sight. It has gone surprisingly smooth, and glitch fixes have been very fast and easy.

comments.author: Correct_Emotion8437
comments.body:
The same thing that stops all the GTA one-shot clones from taking sales from GTA6.  GTA6 isn't even out and those games are free and they still can't get traction.  That's because there is a huge amount of effort put into GTA.  If you put enough effort into your game, it will not be as easy to copy.  

I kind of have a 4 to 1 ratio - just a guessy number that feels right to me.  If it took me 4 weeks to build it, it can be copied in 1 week.  I base this on my own experience re-developing things - so if it took me 4 weeks to build it the first time, it will take me a little less than 1 week to rebuild it now that I know exactly what I'm going for.  It's not perfect because I rarely keep these 1 to 1 . .I usually add something or change something.

comments.author: piXelicidio
comments.body: I'm waiting for someone to clone Factorio and sell it cheaper.

replies.author: More_Setting4514
replies.body:
factorio not made by AI. AI not reach that level.

I talking about game made by AI. If AI can make that game then it can clone that game.

replies.author: piXelicidio
replies.body:
I read your title as “made with AI.” If you're talking about vibe-coding a game, then most likely it won't be a very good game. If you're talking about small, mechanically simple games that unexpectedly become hits, that's nothing new. Flappy Bird, 2048, and many hypercasual games are examples.  
Factorio illustrates very well that really good games aren't easy to copy, because there is more to it than just coding and having a good idea. There is also a lot of testing, feedback, iteration, and polishing over a long period of time.

comments.body: People did this before AI but you are right it is easier now
